on the basis of Article 49 of the Forest Act of 4 October 1991
SR 921.0 (ForA),
and Article 29 of the Environmental Protection Act of 7 October 1983
SR 814.01 ,

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons shall define the parameters according to which a wooded area is defined as forest, within the following ranges:

item.p: area, including an appropriate forest margin: 200–800 m2;
width, including an appropriate forest margin: 10–12 m;
age of stands in newly colonised areas: 10–20 years.

content.p: If the stand fulfils particularly important social or protective functions, it is defined as forest, irrespective of its area, its width or its age.
Wooded pastures are areas consisting of a mosaic of wooded areas and open pastures and which fulfil both livestock husbandry and forestry purposes.
Check dams are structures that hinder the natural flow of water and create a backwater.
The immediate foreground of a check dam is the terrain bordering the installation on the airside. It normally covers a 10-metre-wide strip.

chapter.heading: Protection of the Forest against Intervention

blockList.listIntroduction: The following are not defined as deforestation:

item.p: the use of forest land for forestry buildings and installations and for small structures and installations not used for forestry purposes;

the allocation of forest to a protection zone in accordance with Article 17 of the Spatial Planning Act of 22 June 1979
SR 700 (SPA), if the protection objective is compatible with forest conservation.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No II 17 of the O of 2 Feb. 2000 (Coordination and Simplification of Decision-Making Procedures), in force since 1 March 2000 (AS 2000 703).

content.p: In the case of works for which the Confederation is the competent authority, the deforestation application must be submitted to the lead federal authority, and in the case of works for which the canton is the competent authority, the deforestation application must be submitted to the competent authority under cantonal law.
The authority shall publish the application and provide access to the files for consultation.

The Federal Office for the Environment
The designation of the administrative entity was amended according to Art. 16 para. 3 of the Publication Ordinance of 17 Nov. 2004 (AS 2004 4937). (the FOEN
Name in accordance with No I 5 of the O of 28 Jan. 2015 on the Amendment of Ordinance Law on the Environment, in particular with regard to the programme agreements for the Programme Period 2016–2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2016 (AS 2015 427). This change has been made throughout the text. ) shall issue guidelines on the contents of a deforestation application.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No II 17 of the O of 2 Feb. 2000 (Coordination and Simplification of Decision-Making Procedures), in force since 1 March 2000 (AS 2000 703).

article.heading: Cooperation between the federal authority and the cantons

content.p: If the Confederation is responsible for the deforestation permit, the cooperation between the FOEN and the cantons is subject to Article 49 paragraph 2 ForA. The cantons shall support the federal authorities in the clarification of the facts.

blockList.listIntroduction: Included in the calculation of the deforestation area, based on which the obligation to hear the FOEN (Art. 6 para. 2 ForA) is determined, are all deforestation areas that:

item.p: are included in the deforestation application;
were deforested for the same works in the 15 years previous to the submission of the deforestation application, or for which deforestation is still allowed.

blockList.listIntroduction: The deforestation decision covers the following:

item.p: the areas in which deforestation is authorised or refused and the affected plots with specification of the coordinates;
the nature and scope of the compensatory measures and the affected plots with specification of the coordinates;
the deadlines for the use of the deforestation permit and for the fulfilment of the obligations associated with the deforestation, in particular those involving compensatory measures;
the unresolved objections;
any further conditions and requirements.

content.p:
The FOEN shall keep statistics on the deforestation projects authorised by the Confederation and the cantons. The cantons shall make the necessary information available to the FOEN.
Inserted by No II 17 of the O of 2 Feb. 2000 (Coordination and Simplification of Decision-Making Procedures), in force since 1 March 2000 (AS 2000 703).

article.heading: Compensation in kind
article.subheading:
(Art. 7 para. 1 ForA)
Amended by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, in force since 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

content.p: Compensation in kind is made by creating an area of forest of the same size in a location offering qualitatively similar conditions to the deforested area.
Compensation in kind includes the acquisition of the land, the planting and all of the measures necessary for the long-term safeguarding of the compensatory area.
Areas in which forest is expanding and voluntarily afforested areas which have not yet become forest may be recognised as compensation in kind.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, in force since 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

content.p: The cantons shall designate areas with increasing forest area after consulting the FOEN. Their boundaries shall be based on federal and cantonal surveys, in principle following topographical features and taking account of existing settlements and uses.

article.heading: Conservation of arable land and areas of ecological or landscape value
article.subheading:
(Art. 7 para. 2 let. b ForA)
Amended by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, in force since 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

content.p:
Compensation in kind may be dispensed with in particular in the case of crop rotation areas.
Amended by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, in force since 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

blockList.listIntroduction: Areas of particular ecological value are, in particular:

item.p:
areas designated as nature protection areas in accordance with Article 17 SPA
SR 700 .

blockList.listIntroduction: Areas of particular landscape value are, in particular:

item.p: areas designated as landscape protection zones in accordance with Article 17 SPA.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, in force since 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

content.p: Compensation for deforestation may be dispensed with in the case of projects to guarantee flood protection and the rehabilitation of waters in particular in the case of areas that can no longer be stocked as forest.

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, with effect from 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

article.heading: Record in the land register and notification

blockList.listIntroduction:
At the request of the competent cantonal forest authority, a record must be made in the land register of the obligation to provide:
Amended by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3215).

item.p: compensation in kind or measures for the benefit of nature and landscape conservation;

retrospective compensation for deforestation in the event of a change of use in accordance with Article 7 paragraph 4 ForA.
Amended by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, in force since 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

content.p: The cantons shall monitor all compensatory measures and notify the FOEN of the final approval of the works.

section.heading:
Declaration as Forest
Amended by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, in force since 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

article.heading: Ruling on declaration as forest
article.subheading:
(Art. 10 para. 1 ForA)
Inserted by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, in force since 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

content.p: The ruling on declaration as forest records whether a stocked or unstocked area is a forest or not and specifies its coordinates.
It specifies on a map the location and size of the forest and the location of the affected plots.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, in force since 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

article.heading: Specification of static forest boundaries outside development zones

content.p: Areas where the canton wants to prevent an increase in forest must be specified in the cantonal structure plan.

blockList.listIntroduction: Forest roads may be accessed by motorised vehicular traffic for the following purposes:

item.p: for rescue and recovery purposes;
for police controls;
for military exercises;
for the implementation of measures for the protection against natural events;

item.num:
e.
Amended by No II 61 of the O of 1 Dec. 1997, in force since 1 Jan. 1998 (AS 1997 2779).
item.p: for the maintenance of the network lines of the providers of telecommunications services.

content.p: The rest of the forest may only be accessed by motorised vehicular traffic if such access is unavoidable for the fulfilment of a purpose in accordance with paragraph 1.
Events involving vehicular motorised traffic are prohibited on forest roads and in the rest of the forest.

section.heading:
Buildings and Installations in the Forest
Amended by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, in force since 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, in force since 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

article.heading: Forest structures and installations
article.subheading: (Art. 2 para. 2 let. b and 11 para. 1 ForA)

content.p:
Forest structures and installations, such as forest maintenance depots, log stores, covered wood fuel stores and forest roads may be constructed or altered with official permission in accordance with Article 22 SPA
SR 700 .
Amended by No I of the O of 12 May 2021, in force since 1 July 2021 (AS 2021 294).

blockList.listIntroduction: A requirement for permission is that:

item.p: the structures and installations facilitate regional forest management;
a need is proven for the structures and installations, their location is suitable and their size is adapted to regional conditions; and
there is no overriding public interest in refusing permission.

content.p: Other requirements under federal or cantonal law also apply.

article.heading: Consultation of the cantonal forest authority
article.subheading:
(Art. 11 para. 1 and 16 ForA)
Inserted by No I of the O of 14 June 2013, in force since 1 July 2013 (AS 2013 1983).

content.p:
The granting of permission for the construction of forestry buildings or installations in the forest in accordance with Article 22 SPA
SR 700 is subject to a hearing of the competent cantonal forestry authority.

Exceptional permission for the construction of small structures and installations in the forest that are not used for forestry purposes in accordance with Article 24 SPA may only be granted in agreement with the competent cantonal forestry authority.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex No 4 of the Hydraulic Engineering Ordinance of 25 June 2025, in force since 1 Aug. 2025 (AS 2025 450).

article.heading: Dealing with risks from natural events

content.p: The cantons shall reduce the risks from natural events to an acceptable level and limit such risks in the long term by compiling and evaluating the required basic data and planning and implementing measures in an integrated manner. In doing so, they shall in particular take account of the consequences of climate change and changes in the use of space.

Integrated planning must involve the relevant parties, combine measures in an optimal way and balance interests, in particular those relating to forest management, nature and landscape protection, hydraulic engineering, agriculture and spatial planning.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex No 4 of the Hydraulic Engineering Ordinance of 25 June 2025, in force since 1 Aug. 2025 (AS 2025 450).

blockList.listIntroduction: The FOEN shall compile basic data of national interest on protection against natural events. To this end, it shall:

item.p: conduct surveys on matters relevant to protection against natural events;
keep an inventory on the measures to which the Confederation contributes funding;
analyse events;
prepare reports.

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons shall compile the basic data on protection against natural events on their cantonal territory. To this end, they shall:

item.p: document and analyse events;
document and assess protective structures;
keep a register of events and protective structures;
record the hazards and risks;
prepare hazard assessments and risk maps;
prepare overall plans and, if need be, other higher-level plans.

content.p: They shall designate the hazard areas.
They shall take account of the basic data compiled by the Confederation and its guides on implementation.
They shall submit the risk maps and overall plans regularly in accordance with requirements to the FOEN.
They shall make the compiled basic data available to all interested parties free of charge.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex No 4 of the Hydraulic Engineering Ordinance of 25 June 2025, in force since 1 Aug. 2025 (AS 2025 450).

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons shall take account of the hazard areas and the risks in their structural and land-use plans and in their other activities with a spatial impact. They shall in particular ensure in hazard areas that:

item.p: risks are limited when zoning, upzoning and rezoning and when granting permission for the construction of buildings and installations;
unacceptable risks are reduced by rezoning, downzoning and dezoning or by moving buildings and installations at risk to safer locations.

content.p: They shall designate buffer zones in the structural and land-use plans in which natural events may be allowed to occur in order to protect other areas. In buffer zones, the risk shall be reduced by limiting the form and extent of use.

authorialNote.p: Inserted byAnnex No 4 of the Hydraulic Engineering Ordinance of 25 June 2025, in force since 1 Aug. 2025 (AS 2025 450).

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons shall take organisational measures in order to save human life and to limit damage in the case of an event. To this end, they shall:

item.p: ensure that the operations plans are prepared, practised and familiar to the civilian command staff and emergency services;
ensure that the civilian command staff and emergency services receive specialist advice on preparing for and dealing with natural events;
install and operate the warning systems that are required to ensure the safety of residential areas and transport routes in the case of a natural event;
take the technical measures required to support the emergency services in dealing with natural events.

authorialNote.p: Inserted byAnnex No 4 of the Hydraulic Engineering Ordinance of 25 June 2025, in force since 1 Aug. 2025 (AS 2025 450).

article.heading: Biological and technical measures and buffer zones

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons shall take biological and technical measures to limit the risk of natural events. These measures shall include:

item.p: designating protective forest and creating forest with special protective functions and related young forest maintenance;
silvicultural measures;
structural measures to prevent avalanche damage and the construction of installations for triggering avalanches as a precautionary measure;
rockfall and rockslide barriers and catchment structures, as well as the removal of material at risk of falling;
reinforcement of unstable slopes and gullies and related drainage and erosion protection;
accompanying forest-conservation-related measures in stream channels (stream control works in forests).

content.p: They shall design new protective structures and installations to be robust. They shall assess existing protective structures and installations with regard to their overload capacity and systemic safety and modify them if necessary.

They shall designate buffer zones eligible for compensation, into which natural events are channelled and directed by protective measures in such a way that these areas are exposed more frequently or intensely in order to protect other areas.

chapter.heading: Maintenance and Use of the Forest

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons shall issue regulations for the planning of forest management. These shall define, in particular:

item.p: the types of plans and their content;
the instances responsible for planning;
the planning goals;
how the planning data are acquired and used;
the planning and control procedures;
the regular reviewing of the plans.

content.p: The forestry planning documents must describe, at least, the location conditions as well as the forest functions and their importance.

blockList.listIntroduction: In the case of inter-operational planning, the cantons shall ensure that the population:

item.p: is informed of the goals and progress of the planning;
may be involved in a suitable manner;
may inspect it.

content.p:
They shall take account of the spatial impact of forestry planning in their structural planning.
Inserted by No I 5 of the O of 28 Jan. 2015 on Amendments to the Ordinance Law on the Environment, in particular in relation to the programme agreements for the programme period 2016–2019, in force since 1 March 2015 (AS 2015 427).
All maintenance interventions that contribute to the conservation or restoration of the stability and the quality of a stand are classified as silvicultural measures.

blockList.listIntroduction: Measures carried out as part of young forest maintenance are:

item.num:
a.
Amended by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3215).
item.p: young growth maintenance, thicket maintenance and stem thinning in order to create resistant and adaptable stands suitable to the location;
specific measures to maintain regrowth in selection forests, in other multi-layered forests, in coppices with standards and coppice forests as well as in multi-layered forest margins;
protective measures against damage caused by game;
the creation of paths in areas of difficult access.

blockList.listIntroduction: Thinning and regeneration measures are:

item.p: slash removal and the creation of new stands and the necessary accompanying measures;
wood harvesting and transport.

content.p: Minimum maintenance measures for conserving the protective function of the forest are maintenance interventions that are restricted to ensuring the long-term stability of the stand; felled wood is used locally or left on site, as long as it does not pose a risk.

Clearcutting is the complete or almost complete removal of a stand, which gives rise to ecological conditions similar to those on open lands in the cutting area or causes serious detrimental effects to it or to the nearby stands.
Clearcutting does not arise, if the old stand is cleared following sufficient and secured regeneration.
The cantons shall guarantee the supply of appropriate suitable forest reproductive material.
The competent cantonal forest authority shall select the forests stands, from which forest reproductive material may be obtained. It shall notify the seed stands to the FOEN.
It shall control the commercial and industrial production of seeds and plant parts and issues certificates of origin.
Only forest reproductive material of certified origin may be used for forestry purposes.

blockList.listIntroduction: The FOEN shall advise the cantons about:

item.p: the production, supply and use of forest reproductive material;
the safeguarding of genetic diversity.

content.p: It keeps a register of the seed stands and a register of the genetic reserves.
The import of forest reproductive material requires the authorisation of the FOEN.

blockList.listIntroduction: The authorisation is granted if:

item.p: the forest reproductive material is appropriate for cultivation and its origin is confirmed by an official certificate; or
the importer declares in writing that the reproductive material will be used exclusively outside of the forest.

content.p:
The authorisation to import genetically modified forest reproductive material is regulated by the Release Ordinance of 10 September 2008
SR 814.911 ; the terms of reference of the present Ordinance are also applicable.
Inserted by Art. 51 No 3 of the Plant Protection Ordinance of 28 Feb. 2001 (AS 2001 1191). Amended by Annex 5 No 16 of the Release Ordinance of 10 Sept. 2008, in force since 1 Oct. 2008 (AS 2008 4377).

The Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications
The designation of the administrative entity was amended according to Art. 16 para. 3 of the Publications Ordinance of 17 Nov. 2004 (AS 2004 4937). (DETEC
Name in accordance with No I 5 of the O of 28 Jan. 2015 on the Amendment of Ordinance Law on the Environment, in particular with regard to the programme agreements for the Programme Period 2016–2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2016 (AS 2015 427). This change has been made throughout the text. ) shall enact regulations on the issuing of export documents for forest reproductive material.

Public and private seed extractories, tree nurseries, forest gardens and retailers must keep a record of the origin, processing, breeding and supply of forest reproductive material as well an inventory of such material.
They shall inform the purchasers of forest reproductive material of its classification and origin in their quotations, on their goods and in their invoices.
The FOEN shall control their business management. It may require the assistance of the cantons for this.
DETEC shall issue an ordinance on the implementation of the provisions of this section.
It may allow, for scientific purposes, the import and use of forest reproductive material, the suitability and origin of which are not proven.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No II 21 of the O of 18 May 2005 on the Repeal and Amendment of Ordinances in connection with the Commencement of the Chemicals Act, in force since 1 Aug. 2005 (AS 2005 2695).

content.p:
The exceptional use of environmentally hazardous substances in the forest is governed by the Ordinance on Chemical Risk Reduction of 18 May 2005
SR 814.81 .

article.num:
Art. 26 and 27

section.heading: Prevention and Remediation of Forest Damage

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3215).

blockList.listIntroduction: Forest damage is damage that poses a considerable threat to the function of the forest and that is caused by:

item.p: natural events such as storms, forest fires or drought;
harmful organisms such as certain viruses, bacteria, larvae, insects, fungi or plants.

content.p:
Particularly harmful organisms shall be monitored and controlled in accordance with the provisions of the Plant Health Ordinance of 30 October 2018
SR 916.20 .
Amended by Annex 8 No 7 of the Plant Health Ordinance of 31 Oct. 2018, in force since 1 Jan. 2020 (AS 2018 4209).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3215).

article.heading: Prevention and remediation of forest damage

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons shall take measures to prevent and remediate forest damage, in particular:

item.p: technical and silvicultural measures to prevent and combat fire;
measures to reduce the physical load applied to the soil;
measures to monitor and combat harmful organisms with the aim of eradicating or curbing them or restricting the damage they cause.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3215).

content.p: The FOEN shall establish the principles for the prevention and remediation of forest damage. It shall coordinate the cross-cantonal measures and where necessary shall itself establish such measures.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research (WSL) has the following tasks:

item.p: it organises, together with the cantonal forestry services, the collection of data of relevance to forest protection;
it provides information about the occurrence of harmful organisms and other factors that may damage the forest;
it advises the cantonal forestry services in matters of forest protection.

content.p: Where game damage arises despite the regulation of game populations, a plan shall be developed for its prevention.

The plan shall include forestry measures, hunting measures, measures to improve and protect habitats against disturbance, and a performance review.
Amended by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3215).
The plan is a component of the forestry planning.

chapter.heading:
Training and Basic Data
Amended by Annex 2 No 13 of the O of 21 May 2008 on Geoinformation, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2809).

section.heading: Basic Training and Continuing Education and Training

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2018 (AS 2016 3215).

article.heading: Theoretical and practical basic and continuing education and training

content.p: The FOEN shall ensure, together with the universities, the cantons and other organisations, institutions, and professional associations concerned, that the knowledge and skills acquired during education and training are maintained, and that forestry engineers are introduced to new theoretical and practical advances.

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons shall offer sufficient places for practical continuing education and training and coordinate this offer with each other. Practical continuing education and training shall in particular:

item.p: focus on forest planning, forest management and forest conservation in the context of all forest functions;
aim to improve management skills and administrative knowledge;
be attested by a certificate detailing the acquired skills and knowledge.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex No II 2 of the Vocational and Professional Education and Training Ordinance of 19 Nov. 2003, in force since 1 Jan. 2004 (AS 2003 5047).

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons shall provide:

item.p: the higher vocational training of forest wardens and operate the professional colleges required for this purpose;
together with the responsible organisations, the working environment for the continuing professional education and training of forestry personnel.

content.p:
In accordance with Articles 19 paragraph 1, 28 paragraph 2 and 29 paragraph 3 of the Vocational and Professional Education and Training Act of 13 December 2002
SR 412.10 (VPETA), the enactment or approval of regulations in the field of forestry education and training shall be subject to a hearing of the FOEN.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3215).

content.p: The cantons shall work with agricultural and forestry organisations to organise courses to improve worker safety during wood harvesting for workers with no forestry training.

Federally recognised courses must provide basic skills in worker safety, in particular the correct and safe felling of trees, removal of branches, and the scoring and dragging of trees and tree trunks. Such courses must run for at least 10 days in total.

…
Repealed by No I 7.4 of the O of 9 Nov. 2011 (Review of Extra-Parliamentary Commissions), with effect from 1 Jan. 2012 (AS 2011 5227).
The FOEN shall operate a central coordination and documentation agency for measures concerning forestry education and training.

Section 3

section.heading: Surveys

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3215).

content.p: The FOEN is responsible for the collection of survey data on the forest.

blockList.listIntroduction: In cooperation with the WSL, it surveys:

item.p: by means of the National Forest Inventory, the basic data relating to the locations, functions and condition of the forest;
the long-term development processes in natural forest reserves.

content.p: As part of its basic remit, the WSL shall conduct long-term research programmes to survey the pressure on the forest ecosystem.
The FOEN shall inform the authorities and the general public about these surveys.

section.num:
Section 4
Inserted by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3215).
section.heading: Timber Production

article.heading: Marketing and use of sustainably produced timber

content.p: The marketing and use of sustainably produced timber shall be promoted only in pre-competitive circumstances not relating to one particular company.

In particular, innovative research and development projects that promote sustainable forest management by improving data, opportunities for marketing and use, resource efficiency or public relations may be promoted.
Results and findings relating to the supported activities shall be made available to the FOEN on request.

article.heading: Use of timber in federal buildings and installations

content.p: In the planning, construction and operation of federal buildings and installations the use of timber and timber products shall be promoted.

The sustainability of timber and timber products shall be assessed in accordance with existing guidelines and recommendations such as those issued by the Coordination Group for Construction and Property Services.

chapter.num:
Chapter 6

chapter.heading: Financial Assistance (excluding Investment Credits) and Compensatory Payments

section.heading:
General Provisions
Amended by No 1 5 of the O of 28 Jan. 2015 on the Amendment of Ordinance Law on the Environment, in particular with regard to the programme agreements for the Programme Period 2016–2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2016 (AS 2015 427).

article.heading: General precondition for awarding federal assistance

blockList.listIntroduction: Financial assistance and compensatory payments are only provided by the Confederation if:

item.p: the measures comply with the forestry planning;
the measures are necessary and appropriate;
the measures satisfy the applicable technical, economic and ecological requirements;
the other requirements of federal law are fulfilled;
coordination with the public interests of other sectors is ensured;
further maintenance is guaranteed.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No 1 5 of the O of 28 Jan. 2015 on the Amendment of Ordinance Law on the Environment, in particular with regard to the programme agreements for the Programme Period 2016–2019 (AS 2015 427). Amended by Annex No 4 of the Hydraulic Engineering Ordinance of 25 June 2025, in force since 1 Aug. 2025 (AS 2025 450).

content.p: In order to receive compensatory payments, costs are allowable only if they are actually incurred and are directly required for the proper fulfilment of the task for which a contribution is due.

blockList.listIntroduction: The costs of the following are allowable for compensatory payments pursuant to Articles 39 paragraphs 1 and 2 and 40 paragraph 1 letter c:

item.p: compiling the basic data and planning measures;
implementing measures;
acquiring land, easements and formal and de facto expropriation;
marking.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following in particular are not allowable with regard to compensatory payments pursuant to Article 39 paragraphs 1 and 2:

item.p: any fees incurred;
costs that can be passed on to the person responsible for the cost being incurred;
the cost of creating significant added value that is generated independently of the protection against natural events provided by the measures;
the cost of measures that improve the protection of national roads against natural events and are already covered by the contribution to costs from the Federal Roads Office;
administrative costs.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following in particular are not allowable with regard to compensatory payments pursuant to Article 40 paragraph 1 letter c and paragraph 3:

item.p: any fees incurred;
costs that can be passed on to third parties who are significant beneficiaries or responsible to a significant extent for the cost being incurred.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex No 4 of the Hydraulic Engineering Ordinance of 25 June 2025, in force since 1 Aug. 2025 (AS 2025 450).

blockList.listIntroduction: Compensatory payments for compiling basic data and for the measures, with the exception of payments under paragraph 2, are allocated on a global basis. The level of the global compensatory payments shall be specified by the FOEN and the canton concerned in programme agreements and is based on:

item.p: the risk of natural events;
the extent, impact and quality of the measures.

blockList.listIntroduction: Compensatory payments may be awarded on a case-by-case basis if the measures:

item.p: have a supracantonal dimension;
concern protected areas or objects listed in national inventories;
require particularly complex or expert assessment due to the possible alternatives or for other reasons; or
were an unforeseeable necessity.

content.p: The contribution to the allowable costs of compiling basic data amounts to 50 per cent.

blockList.listIntroduction: The contribution to the allowable costs of measures amounts to between 35 and 45 per cent and is dependent on:

item.p: the work involved in compiling the basic data;
the extent, impact and quality of the measures.

blockList.listIntroduction: The contribution pursuant to paragraph 4 may in exceptional cases be increased by up to 20 per cent if a canton incurs substantial costs for exceptional protective measures against natural events, in particular those taken following damage caused by bad weather. The contribution depends on:

item.p: the necessity of the measures as a consequence of the extraordinary situation;
the substantial financial burden on the canton concerned caused by taking protective measures against natural hazards;
the plan in its entirety.

blockList.listIntroduction: No compensatory payments shall be made for:

item.p: measures required to protect buildings and installations which at the time of construction were in already designated hazard zones or known hazard areas and are not necessarily attached to that location;
measures to protect tourist buildings and installations, such as cableways, ski lifts, ski runs or hiking trails, that are situated outside of the inhabited area;
compiling data and implementing measures in the structural and land-use plans and in other activities with a spatial impact;
making technical arrangements for emergency operations and expenditure on management staff and emergency services that is covered by their basic mandate;
taking technical measures;
drawing up cantonal working aids, directives and guidelines.

blockList.listIntroduction: The level of the global compensatory payments awarded for measures required to enable the protective forest to fulfil its protective function is based on:

item.p: hazard and damage potential;
the number of hectares of the protective forest to be maintained;
the scope and the planning of the infrastructure required for the maintenance of the protective forest;
the quality of the services provided.

content.p: The amount is negotiated between the FOEN and the canton concerned.

The contribution awarded by ruling to the costs of projects resulting from exceptional natural events shall not exceed 40 per cent of the costs and shall be in accordance with paragraph 1 letters a, c and d.
Inserted by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3215).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3215). See also the transitional provisions to these amendments at the end of this text.

article.heading: Measures against forest damage outside the protective forest

blockList.listIntroduction: The level of the global compensatory payments for measures to prevent and mitigate forest damage outside the protective forest is determined by:

item.p: the degree of threat to forest functions;
the number of hectares over which measures are taken;
the quality of the services.

content.p: The FOEN and the cantons concerned shall negotiate the amount.

Compensatory payments may be made in individual cases in which the measures were unforeseeable and particularly costly. The amount shall not exceed 40 per cent of the costs and is determined in accordance with paragraph 1 letters a and c.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 17 Aug. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3215).

content.p: Compensation may be paid in cases of hardship if individuals are particularly badly affected and cannot be expected to meet the cost of the damage themselves.

Applications for compensation are to be submitted, with reasons given, once the damage has been ascertained but no later than one year after the measures have been put in place by the competent cantonal authorities.
No compensation is paid for loss of yield or immaterial damage.
The Confederation shall reimburse the cantons between 35 and 50 per cent of the cost of compensation in accordance with the provision on global compensatory payments in Article 40a.

It may award financial assistance to organisations for the promotion and coordination of research and development, on a case-by-case basis and equal to at most the funding provided by third parties, provided it receives an adequate right of co-decision in these organisations.

section.heading: Procedure for Granting Global Compensatory Payments or Financial Assistance

content.p: The canton shall submit the application for global compensatory payments or financial assistance to the FOEN.

blockList.listIntroduction: The application shall contain details of:

item.p: the programme objectives to be achieved;
the measures probably required to achieve the objectives and their implementation;
the effectiveness of the measures.

content.p: In the case of measures that affect more than one canton, the cantons shall ensure the coordination of the applications with the other cantons concerned.
The FOEN shall enter into a programme agreement with the competent cantonal authority.

blockList.listIntroduction: The subject matter of the programme agreement is in particular:

item.p: the strategic programme objectives to be jointly achieved;
the services to be provided by the canton;
the contribution to be paid by the Confederation;
controlling.

content.p: The programme agreement shall have a maximum term of four years.
The FOEN shall issue guidelines on the procedure for programme agreements and on the information and documents required in connection with the subject matter of the programme agreement.
Global compensatory payments or financial assistance are paid in instalments.
The canton shall provide the FOEN with a report each year on the use of the global subsidies.

blockList.listIntroduction: The FOEN shall control by random sample:

item.p: the implementation of individual measures in accordance with the programme objectives;
the use of the subsidies paid.

blockList.listIntroduction: The FOEN shall withhold the instalment payments during the programme in full or in part if the canton:

item.p: fails to comply with its reporting obligation (Art. 49 para. 1);
culpably causes serious disruption to its own services.

content.p: If it becomes apparent after the programme that the services provided are substandard, the FOEN shall require the canton to rectify the defects; it shall allow the canton an appropriate period within which to do this.

If installations or equipment for which financial assistance or compensatory payments have been provided are used for a purpose other than that intended, the FOEN may require the canton to arrange for the non-intended use to be stopped or reversed within a reasonable period.

If the defects are not rectified or the non-intended use is not stopped or reversed, the recovery of the payments made is governed by Articles 28 and 29 of the Subsidies Act of 5 October 1990
SR 616.1 .

section.heading: Procedure for Providing Compensatory Payments or Financial Assistance in Specific Cases

content.p: Applications for compensatory payments or financial assistance in specific cases without the involvement of a canton must be submitted to the FOEN; all other applications must be submitted to the canton.

The canton shall examine the applications that it receives and pass them on to the FOEN with a justified proposal, the cantonal authorisations already available and the cantonal decision on the subsidy.
The FOEN shall issue guidelines on the information and documents required in connection with the application.
The FOEN shall issue a ruling determining the amount of the compensatory payment or the financial assistance or shall enter into an agreement with the recipient of the subsidy.
Payment of subsidies shall be dependent on the progress made with the measures.

If, despite receiving a warning, a recipient, whose application for compensatory payments or financial assistance has been approved, fails to carry out the measures or carries them in a substandard manner, the compensatory payments or financial assistance shall not be paid out or shall be reduced.

If compensatory payments or financial assistance have been paid out and if, despite receiving a warning, the recipient fails to carry out the measures or carries them out in a substandard manner, the recovery of the payments made is governed by Article 28 of the Subsidies Act of 5 October 1990
SR 616.1 .

If installations or equipment for which compensatory payments or financial assistance have been paid out are not used for the intended purpose, the FOEN may require the canton to arrange for the non-intended use to be stopped or reversed within a reasonable period.
If the non-intended use is not stopped or reversed, the recovery of the payments made is governed by Articles 28 and 29 of the Subsidies Act of 5 October 1990.
Article 49 applies by analogy to reporting and controlling.

blockList.listIntroduction: Investment credits shall be granted if:

item.p: the investment is necessary and suitable to protect against natural events or for the maintenance and use of the forest; and
the investment is required due to the applicant's financial circumstances.

content.p: The applicant must be able to support the total financial burden.
The applicant must exhaust his or her own financial resources and claim any contributions available from third parties.

Investment credits may not be accumulated with credits granted under the Federal Act of 23 March 1962
[AS 1962 1273, 1972 2699, 1977 2249 No I 961, 1991 362 No II 52 857 Annex No 27, 1992 288 Annex No 47 2104. AS 1998 3033 Annex let. f] on Agricultural Investment Credits and Business Subsidies or the Federal Act of 28 June 1974
[AS 1975 392, 1980 1798, 1985 387, 1991 857 Annex No 24, 1992 288 Annex No 43. AS 1997 2995 Art. 25]. See now: the FA of 6 Oct. 2006 on Regional Policy (SR 901.0). on Investment Subsidies for Mountain Regions.
The cantons are not entitled to credits for their own investments.

...

The FOEN shall grant the canton global loans to cover the payment of investment credits. The loans shall be interest free and repayable over 20 years.
The canton shall notify the FOEN each year of its probable borrowing requirements for the coming year.

The available funds are allocated according to demand.
Amended by No I 21 of the O of 7 Nov. 2007 on the New System of Financial Equalisation and Division of Tasks between the Confederation and the Cantons, in force since 1 Jan. 2008 (AS 2007 5823).
Applications for investment credits must be submitted to the canton.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following documents must be enclosed with each application:

item.p: the general operational plan;
the operating accounts;
a report on the applicant's financial circumstances.

content.p: Companies that are commercially contracted to maintain or use the forest must include the balance sheets and profit and loss accounts for the last two years in their application.

article.heading: Amount of credit and rate of interest

content.p: Investment credits are normally interest free. However, if the applicant can support the total financial burden, an appropriate rate of interest shall be charged.
